notes: Two findings beyond the original hypothesis, both important for the write-up: (1) the val set contains NO frames with 1-2 fish (minimum is k=3) -- the sparse-frame regime H7 worried about is entirely untested by this dataset, not merely 'found to be rare'; extrapolated (untested) independence-approximation miss risk at k=1 is ~22-28% depending on which recall figure is used, a real quantified gap to flag. (2) model.val(conf=X) does NOT pin box.mp/box.mr to conf=X for X below the internal argmax (methodological trap, documented) -- reading the fine-grained per-confidence curve directly revealed the DEPLOYED operating point (conf=0.20) actually runs at P=0.720/R=0.782, not the headline P=0.858/R=0.719. Production recall is thus HIGHER (more reassuring for full-frame-miss risk) than the number the paper has been citing for this discussion; the paper's H7 section should cite the deployed-point recall (0.782), not the academic-argmax headline (0.719), when discussing real-world full-frame-miss risk.
